# How to use this booklet {.unnumbered}

This is the exercise booklet for **Module 3** of the Health Data Science MSc.
It is organised by teaching day: each day is a part of the book, and each
chapter inside a day is one exercise you can finish in a single sitting.

**Each exercise is code to read and copy.** The worked examples are shown with
the output they produce, so you can compare your own result against ours. You run
the code in R or Python on your own machine or vlab.  

Some tasks appear as code containing `______` for you to fill in. They are shown but not run, which is why no output appears beneath them.

## Why both languages

Most health data science teams use one language for data management and the
other for modelling, and the ability to read a colleague's code in the language
you do not prefer is worth more than fluency in either. Every exercise therefore
has an R path and a Python path doing the same work. They will apear with differentiated tabs and difefrentiated colours (blue for R and orange for Python). Pick which one to use, in class we will be going through R most of the times. Pay attention to where both differ!


## Worked answers

The answer to each task, with its output, is published after the session it
belongs to. 

## The data you will work with

These files sit in `data/`. Each is introduced in the exercise that first uses
it, with what it holds, the clinical question it stands in for, and what is
wrong with it.

| File | What it is |
|------|------------|
| [`los_data.csv`](data/los_data.csv) | 1000 admissions: length of stay against age and severity |
| [`los_data_skewed.csv`](data/los_data_skewed.csv) | the same admissions with a realistic right-skewed stay |
| [`extract_A`](data/extract_A.csv) / [`B`](data/extract_B.csv) / [`C.csv`](data/extract_C.csv) | three later monthly extracts from the same service |
| [`birthweight.csv`](data/birthweight.csv) | 600 births: birthweight against gestational age |
| [`diabetes.csv`](data/diabetes.csv) | 768 adults screened for type 2 diabetes, eight measurements |
| [`longisland_heart.csv`](data/longisland_heart.csv) | 200 cardiac assessments, 14 columns, a graded outcome |
| [`bupa.csv`](data/bupa.csv) | 345 patients, five liver blood tests and a daily alcohol count |
| [`gapminder.csv`](data/gapminder.csv) | 1,704 country-years: life expectancy, population and GDP per capita |
| [`messy_gp_patients.csv`](data/messy_gp_patients.csv) | 30 GP patients whose age, height, practice and smoking status need cleaning |
| [`hospital_admissions.csv`](data/hospital_admissions.csv) | 250 emergency and elective admissions with gaps in creatinine and smoking status |
| [`creatinine_truth.csv`](data/creatinine_truth.csv) | the real creatinine for 18 of those admissions, kept back for the imputation exercise |

Each filename above links to that single file. A browser may show a `.csv`
as text rather than saving it, so use right-click ▸ *Save Link As* — or take
all of them at once, which is the easier route:

### Download it before the first session

[**hds-m3-data.zip**](hds-m3-data.zip) — every file above.

Unzip it **inside the folder you will write your scripts in**, so that you end
up with this:

```
my-hds-m3/
├── exercise1.R          <- your own script, whatever you call it
└── data/
    ├── los_data.csv
    ├── diabetes.csv
    └── ...
```

Every path in the booklet is written as `data/los_data.csv`, relative to the
folder your script is in. If you unzip it somewhere else, `read_csv()` will
tell you the file does not exist — and the fix is to move the `data` folder
next to your script rather than to edit the path in the code.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
In RStudio or Positron, make that folder a **project** (File ▸ New Project, or
`.Rproj`) and your working directory is set correctly every time you open it.
In plain Python, run your script from that folder rather than from elsewhere.
:::
